questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: How a blocking power works
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a permanent member blocks a resolution
questions.stem: Explain how a single permanent member can block a Security Council resolution.

answer.exemplar: A permanent member casting a negative vote on a substantive resolution vetoes it, so no binding decision can pass even if all other members agree, which protects that power's interests.

questions.explanation: The veto lets one permanent member stop any substantive resolution, protecting its interests and often paralysing action. Tempting answers confuse veto with abstention.
